Article Title: 'Incompatible with secular character': Centre tells Delhi HC mosque inside Krishi Bhawan must be demolished
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Tuesday informed the Delhi high court that it is planning to remove a mosque situated within the Krishi Bhawan complex to facilitate the redevelopment and reconstruction of the Common Central Secretariat under the Central Vista project.In a status report filed through the Land and Development Office, the Centre also submitted that Krishi Bhawan and the Central Secretariat complex are secular public premises dedicated exclusively to administrative functions. It said the establishment or retention of a permanent religious structure within a central government office complex would be incompatible with the secular character of government property.The Centre maintained that Qadeemi Masjid stands on government-owned land and that its caretaking committee was granted only permissive possession of the premises under an agreement executed on November 8, 1940.The government also claimed that the agreement did not confer any ownership rights, title or interest in the property upon the managing committee.The agreement contained a provision empowering government authorities to take back possession of the property in the event of any breach or default in complying with its terms and conditions.The Centre has relied on an agreement dated November 8, 1940, executed between the then government, as the owner of the property, and the secretary of the managing committee of Jama Masjid.Under the agreement, the government had granted permissive possession of the premises to the committee exclusively for use as a mosque.The agreement also imposed several restrictions on the use and modification of the property, prohibiting the managing committee from making alterations, undertaking repairs to the existing buildings, constructing graves or raising any new structure, even temporarily, without obtaining prior written approval from the government.Mosque required to be removed for execution of Central Vista projectThe Centre said the removal of the structure was necessary as the Central Vista Redevelopment Master Plan provides for the redevelopment and reconstruction of Common Central Secretariat Buildings 4 and 5 at Plot No. 120, covering the existing sites of Shastri Bhawan and Krishi Bhawan.According to the status report, the proposed project is aimed at modernising infrastructure considered essential for the country's governance and administrative functioning. The government has asserted that the mosque presently stands within the identified project site and is required to be removed for the execution of the proposed construction.Describing the construction of CCS Buildings 4 and 5 as a public project of paramount national importance, the Centre also argued that retaining the mosque or reserving any portion of the project site for the religious structure would be inconsistent with the redevelopment master plan.The L&DO has further argued that public land situated in a central administrative zone cannot be permanently reserved for a religious structure.Based on these submissions, the Centre has maintained that the managing committee cannot claim a right to compel the government to allot or earmark a separate portion of land for the mosque within the Krishi Bhawan compound or the Central Secretariat complex.The government has also disputed any violation of the fundamental right to freedom of religion guaranteed under Article 25 of the Constitution.It has submitted that the constitutional provision does not confer a right to insist on worship at a particular place on government land held under a permissive arrangement.The government's response comes in reply to a petition filed by Qadeemi Masjid through its caretaking committee, challenging the proposed action concerning the religious structure.The petition further states that the Delhi Waqf Board notified the property as Waqf property in 1970 and recorded its antiquity.The petitioners claimed that even after Krishi Bhawan, Shastri Bhawan and surrounding government offices were constructed in the 1950s and 1960s, the mosque continued to exist and was used by Muslim employees of the offices for offering prayers.The petitioners acknowledged that the land underneath the mosque is government property but expressed apprehension over the ongoing redevelopment, which involves dismantling the existing complex.They maintained that they have no objection to the Central Vista redevelopment project and are not seeking a suspension or delay in the construction of the Common Central Secretariat buildings.
Article Summary: The Centre is planning to remove a mosque situated within the Krishi Bhawan complex to facilitate the redevelopment of the Common Central Secretariat under the Central Vista project. The Centre said the establishment or retention of a permanent religious structure within a central government office complex would be incompatible with the secular character of government property.

Article Title: Ex-Air chief AP Singh wrote to Rajnath, urged him to keep Race Course land under IAF control
Article Text:

IAF flags operational concerns

'Absolute disgrace': Congress slams Centre over reclaiming IAF complex

Centre's drive to reclaim prime land

NEW DELHI: Days before retiring as chief of air staff, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh wrote to defence minister Rajnath Singh , raising concerns over the sealing of the Indian Air Force's (IAF) sports complex at the Race Course Air Force Station in New Delhi.In a letter dated October 26, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh urged the defence minister to ensure that the over 40-acre land parcel remained under the Air Force's control, news agency PTI reported, citing people familiar with the matter.AP Singh also raised the issue during an in-person meeting with Rajnath Singh on October 29, three days before his retirement on October 31. He sought the minister's intervention after authorities under the ministry of housing and urban affairs (MoHUA) sealed the sports complex, triggering concern within defence circles, as reported by PTI.The sealing of the facility, which includes a golf course, swimming pool and other amenities, also led to the cancellation of a planned farewell for the outgoing Air Chief Marshal.There has been no official statement from either the IAF or the defence ministry on the matter.In his letter, AP Singh referred to a joint survey of the land parcel conducted in 2014 by the then ministry of urban development, the Defence Estate Department and the Air Force.He argued that the land should remain with the IAF, citing the sports complex's important role in the overall functioning of the air station.The Air Force has also conveyed its objections to the defence ministry and sought the cancellation of the sealing process, the people said.It has highlighted the operational importance of the Race Course Air Force Station, particularly its role in addressing potential aerial security threats in the high-security zone around the Prime Minister's residence.AP Singh also referred to the station's history and its existing land arrangement in his communication. The complex comprises three distinct segments of land, and he stressed that all its facilities should continue to function as usual.The Congress on Tuesday criticised the Centre's move to reclaim the land housing the Indian Air Force Sports Complex, accusing the Modi government of showing "utter disrespect" to the IAF community.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report on X which said that Air Chief Marshal AP Singh had written to defence minister Rajnath Singh.In his post, Ramesh said, "The IAF Sports Complex has a long history and has, over the decades, served many public purposes, as well as being an integral part of the Indian Air Force social infrastructure.""The Modi government's actions are an absolute disgrace and show utter disrespect to the entire IAF family," Ramesh added.The sealing is part of a wider government exercise to reclaim high-value land parcels in the vicinity of Lok Kalyan Marg.Over the past several weeks, the land and development Office (L&DO), under the Union housing and urban affairs ministry, has reviewed plots being used for defence golf courses and sports facilities.The ministry had earlier asked the concerned authorities to hand over the land housing the Air Force Golf Course. The L&DO subsequently issued eviction notices to the sports complex's management, seeking the return of the land.The government has also taken action against other establishments occupying prime land in the area.In August, the department evicted the Delhi Race Club from its 53-acre premises on Lok Kalyan Marg, citing the requirement of the land for an unspecified public purpose.It also reclaimed the Jaipur Polo Ground from the India Polo Association, citing broader public purposes, governance and defence infrastructure projects.
Article Summary: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh wrote to defence minister Rajnath Singh. He raised concerns over the sealing of the Indian Air Force's sports complex. The complex includes a golf course, swimming pool and other amenities. sealing is part of a wider government exercise to reclaim high-value land parcels.

Article Title: 'Huge impact on polls': IB opposes shifting convict in ex-Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassination to state jail
Article Text:
Ex-Punjab CM murdered on August 31, 1995

Why is Hawara seeking a transfer?

NEW DELHI: The Intelligence Bureau (IB) on Tuesday opposed the transfer of Jagtar Singh Hawara, convicted in the 1995 assassination of then-Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, from Delhi's Tihar Jail to a prison in Punjab, telling the Supreme Court that the move could have a “huge impact” on the upcoming assembly elections in the state.The agency also classified Hawara as a high-risk prisoner and said he should not be shifted to Punjab. A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and P B Varale described the IB report as “very damning” while hearing Hawara's plea seeking a transfer to a prison in his home state.Senior advocate S Muralidhar, appearing for Hawara, told the court, “If elections are a concern, this may be taken up after three months.” The Supreme Court posted the matter for hearing in February next year. Elections to the 117-member Punjab Assembly are due early next year.Beant Singh, who served as Punjab chief minister from 1992 to 1995, was killed in a suicide bombing outside the state civil secretariat in Chandigarh on August 31, 1995. The blast also killed 16 others. Hawara, a member of the banned Babbar Khalsa International, was convicted in the assassination case and is serving a life sentence for the remainder of his natural life.Hawara's plea argues that he is a native of Punjab's Fatehgarh Sahib district and should be allowed to serve his sentence in a prison in the state. It also says there are no cases pending against him in Delhi and that his conduct in prison has been without blemish, apart from a jailbreak in January 2004.Hawara was among four inmates who escaped from Chandigarh's high-security Burail Jail on January 22, 2004, by digging a nearly 100-foot-long tunnel. The other escapees were Paramjit Singh Bheora, Jagtar Singh Tara and Devi Singh. Hawara and Bheora were subsequently arrested, while Tara was caught in Thailand. Devi Singh remains absconding.Opposing the transfer, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Delhi government, had earlier told the Supreme Court that Hawara's jailbreak history raised the risk of another escape. She also cited a Union home ministry advisory on the transfer of high-risk prisoners and the Punjab government's concerns over the possible impact on law and order.Hawara was sentenced to death by a trial court in March 2007. The Punjab and Haryana High Court commuted the sentence to life imprisonment in October 2010, directing that he should not be released for the rest of his life. Appeals against the high court verdict are pending before the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Jagtar Singh Hawara was convicted in the 1995 assassination of then-Punjab chief minister Beant Singh. Hawara is serving a life sentence for the remainder of his natural life. He is seeking a transfer to a prison in his home state of Punjab. Elections to the 117-member Punjab Assembly are due early next year.

NEW DELHI: In a major setback to the ruling National Conference in Jammu and Kashmir , Srinagar Lok Sabha member Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi on Tuesday formally announced his resignation from the parliamentary seat and party on the 26th death anniversary of his father.Mehdi hinted at forming a new political party led by "honest and compassionate people," as news agency PTI reported.A day earlier, banners at the entrance of Mehdi's residence in Srinagar had offered a glimpse of the message he wanted to convey. One read, “Wada kursi se bada hai” (a promise is bigger than a chair), while the other said, “Kirdar ki siyasat, usoolon ki siyasat” (politics of character, politics of principles).One party worker said, “even at a barber's shop, people do not give up their chairs for someone else even if that person is older. Here is a man willing to leave his chair for the sake of principles. Who gives up a chair like that.”Mehdi's resignation comes amid growing discontent within the ruling party, with Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah facing a revolt by a section of NC legislators.Around 25 legislators have reportedly demanded the replacement of all eight cabinet ministers, including the deputy chief minister, within 15 days.They have also sought the removal of Nasir Aslam Wani, Omar Abdullah's close aide and political adviser.At a meeting held at the residence of NC MLA Qaiser Jamshaid Lone on Friday evening, the legislators passed a resolution seeking a cabinet overhaul and wider consultations within the party before portfolios are allocated.Around 18 MLAs attended the meeting in person, while seven joined online, according to a legislator who was present.The NC has 41 MLAs in the 90-member Jammu and Kashmir assembly. It runs a coalition government with the support of six Congress MLAs, six independent legislators and one CPM member.
Article Summary: Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi formally announced his resignation from the parliamentary seat and party on the 26th death anniversary of his father. Mehdi hinted at forming a new political party led by "honest and compassionate people" Mehdi's resignation comes amid growing discontent within the ruling party.

Article Title: At Anant Ambani’s Vantara, global zoos turn to shared data to protect wildlife
Article Text: The EARAZA Annual Conference 2026 concluded at Vantara in Jamnagar, bringing together wildlife professionals, veterinarians, scientists and conservation leaders from 98 institutions across 30 countries, along with representatives of 29 Indian zoological institutions.Held under the theme “Strengthening Global Partnerships for Wildlife Conservation”, the four-day conference focused on cross-border conservation programmes, animal welfare, wildlife medicine, technology, crisis response and public engagement.The conference opened on October 26 with a performance by three-time Grammy Award-winning composer and environmentalist Ricky Kej. The inauguration was followed by a traditional lamp-lighting ceremony attended by Vivaan Karani, CEO, Vantara; Svetlana Akulova, president, EARAZA; Prof Raman Sukumar of the Indian Institute of Science; Dr V Clement Ben, member secretary, Central Zoo Authority; and Dr Brij Kishor Gupta, director, Gujarat Zoological Research and Rescue Centre.The Indian Zoo Yearbook, Volume 11, 2026, was also released during the opening ceremony.As host, Vantara announced that the ANTZ Software Platform would be offered free of cost to all EARAZA members for one year. ANTZ is a zoological management platform with an Open Data Exchange that enables participating institutions to share information across the network.The announcement aligned with one of the conference's key themes: the need for conservation knowledge and data to move more easily between institutions and across national borders. Akulova spoke about the importance of creating global data infrastructure for biodiversity conservation, allowing information generated by one institution to inform decisions elsewhere.The sessions covered coordinated conservation programmes for the Amur tiger, Oriental stork, Blakiston’s eagle-owl and great bustard. Discussions also examined the conservation breeding of Boiga snakes, the reintroduction of the long-eared hedgehog, the conservation of the Indian wild ass and the ex-situ conservation of the Amur tiger.The second day focused on coexistence, urban biodiversity and public engagement. Sessions examined snake conservation and snakebite prevention, biodiversity conservation in million-plus cities and the role of citizen science.A panel on “Animal Welfare: From Inputs to Measurable Outcomes”, moderated by Karani, discussed how care practices can be assessed through measurable outcomes for individual animals. Other sessions addressed the visitor experience at zoological institutions, conservation education and the role of mass media. Wildlife biologist and television presenter Forrest Galante spoke about taking conservation conversations to wider audiences.Delegates also discussed crisis management in wildlife-care facilities and disaster response in the wild. Presentations covered polar bear rescue, wildlife disease diagnostics, animal nutrition and the work of zoological institutions in Russia. Padma Shri awardee Dr K K Sarma, known for his work with elephants, shared field perspectives on human-wildlife conflict.The conference also included interactive formats such as “The Elephant in the Room”, where delegates reflected on difficult questions facing the zoological sector, and the Solution Station, which invited professionals to bring real challenges in wildlife care and conservation for expert guidance.Technology and research took centre stage on the third day. Vantara presented tools developed under the ANTZ platform, including Vespr, an edge-AI bioacoustic monitor that identifies species on the device; Smart Egg Analysis, which helps teams measure and monitor eggs; and an NFC-enabled system for digitally recording animal-care rounds.Scientific presentations by Vantara experts covered non-invasive population genomics of Asiatic lions, paraveterinary training, avian rewilding, the use of artificial intelligence to understand animals and efforts to bridge ex-situ and in-situ conservation.Alongside the sessions, the conference featured an exhibition with 13 exhibitors from seven countries. The displays included veterinary technologies, wildlife diagnostics, genomics, automated microscopy, assisted reproduction systems, avian incubation equipment and remote drug-delivery solutions. Vantara’s host pavilions also featured innovations in wildlife care, nutrition, architecture and technology, along with a virtual reality experience.The final day focused on science-based care for rescued Asian elephants, animal nutrition in rescue and rewilding, habitat change, cryopreservation, triage and parasite surveillance. Dr Manilal Valliyate, chief communication officer at Vantara, moderated a panel on veterinary capacity-building.The conference concluded with a gala dinner and closing ceremony, where Lifetime Achievement Awards were presented to six leaders from India and abroad: Svetlana Akulova, René Franěk, Azer Huseynov, S C Sharma, Dr D N Singh and Dr B S Bonal.The EARAZA flag was then handed over to China, host of the 2027 conference. The event concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr Brij Kishor Gupta.
Article Summary: The EARAZA Annual Conference 2026 concluded at Vantara in Jamnagar, India. It brought together wildlife professionals, veterinarians, scientists and conservation leaders from 98 institutions across 30 countries. The four-day conference focused on cross-border conservation programmes, animal welfare, wildlife medicine, technology, crisis response and public engagement.

Article Title: 'Gaddar': BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of treason, calls him 'Bhasmasur'

'They want to overthrow elected governments': BJP targets opposition

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Tuesday launched a scathing attack on Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi , accusing him of treason, promoting anarchy and attempting to undermine India's democratic institutions.BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia labelled Rahul Gandhi 'gaddar' (traitor) and 'Bhasmasur', alleging that his political approach was aimed at destabilising the country and weakening its constitutional framework.Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Bhatia questioned Rahul Gandhi's foreign engagements, raised allegations over the Congress's memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Communist Party of China (CCP) and demanded answers about the alleged funding of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."This issue is about the model of anarchy, disorder, and treason that the Leader of the Opposition is presenting to the country... That is why he is being referred to as 'Rahul Gaddar'," Bhatia said.He also accused Rahul of advocating unconstitutional regime change and attempting to weaken democratic institutions.Bhatia described Rahul Gandhi as a destructive force and accused him of promoting anarchy instead of respecting India's democratic framework."If India has one greatest strength, it lies in its democratic government, its reverence for the Constitution, and the stability it has maintained for 12 years. On the other hand, there is an opposition that is anarchic in its thinking, anti-Constitution, and openly speaks of overthrowing the government. Rahul Gandhi believes in anarchy and destruction; it is not for nothing that he is called a 'Bhasmasura' (a destructive force). He has become the kind of leader who seeks to usher in anarchy by killing democracy, strangling it to death," he said.The BJP spokesperson alleged that the opposition was seeking to overthrow elected governments and undermine constitutional institutions, including Parliament and the Supreme Court."The other ideology says that whatever you build, our only task is to destroy it. That is why Rahul Gandhi is not called Bhasmasur without reason. If anyone is attempting to destroy these institutions, it is Rahul Gandhi," he said.Bhatia also targeted Gandhi, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and former Bihar deputy chief minister Tejashwi Yadav over their alleged support for regime change.He warned that repeated calls for regime change could instead turn public opinion against the opposition and threaten the political future of its leaders."I say this with a lot of responsibility: people wanting a regime change might witness a situation where the people of the country feel that the Opposition is irresponsible and should be changed. The public will find an alternative to the opposition; do not imagine, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee, or Tejashwi Yadav, that you will gain anything through anarchy. This public will put an end to your political careers. India’s democracy will remain unscathed," he said.The remarks came amid a controversy over the use of the phrase 'regime change' by senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora and Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera during public statements and press conferences in Delhi.The comments were made in the context of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Bhatia also questioned Rahul Gandhi's meetings with foreign figures, including US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar and Mushfiqul Fazal, whom he accused of adopting anti-India positions."How can the leader of opposition in India be anti-India? How can he betray the nation?... The central question is why Rahul Gandhi is meeting individuals like Ilhan Omar or Mushfiqul Fazal who adopt anti-India stances. Is there any discussion about weakening India and bringing about regime change?" he asked.He further demanded that Gandhi disclose the contents of the Congress's MoU with the Communist Party of China and explain the alleged funding behind protests."Rahul Gandhi signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Communist Party of China (CCP) but has not disclosed what it contains to this day... He must also clarify where the funding for these protests, which are being organized with the aim of creating anarchy, is coming from."The BJP spokesperson also accused Gandhi of inappropriate physical conduct with a woman police officer during an anti-CEC protest on Ashoka Road near Jantar Mantar."Rahul Gandhi's inappropriate touching of a woman police officer is disgraceful. No political position gives anyone the right to touch a woman inappropriately. He must answer for his shameful behaviour," Bhatia said.He argued that Gandhi's position as Leader of the Opposition did not give him the right to behave inappropriately with security personnel.In his concluding remarks, Bhatia accused Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders of attempting to weaken India's democratic institutions and destabilise elected governments."Wherever there is an elected government, they want to overthrow it. They want to destroy constitutional institutions such as the Supreme Court and Parliament, as well as historical monuments," he said.The BJP leader maintained that India's democratic framework and constitutional institutions would remain strong despite what he described as the opposition's attempts to create disorder.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia labelled Rahul Gandhi 'gaddar' (traitor) and 'Bhasmasur' Alleges that his political approach was aimed at destabilising the country and weakening its constitutional framework. Accuses Rahul of advocating unconstitutional regime change and attempting to weaken democracy.

Article Title: Indian national killed as helicopters collide near Mount Everest in Nepal
Article Text:
An official said that one helicopter was travelling from Lukla, while the other was returning from Gorakhpur, near the Everest base camp. Both reportedly attempted to land at the same spot.

Who were injured in the collision?

Who were inside the helicopters

Where did the accident take place?

An Indian national was killed and three others, including a New Zealand resident of Indian origin, were injured in a helicopter crash in Nepal. The two helicopters collided while attempting to land near Mount Everest in Nepal on Tuesday morning.The accident took place at around 8.11am (local time) at Pheriche in Ward 4 of Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality in Solukhumbu district.A video of the incident has captured the moment the two aircraft collided, highlighting the dangers of helicopter operations in the busy Everest region.Nepal Police confirmed the casualties from the accident in a statement. They said, "Solukhumbu accident further update: One person dead, three injured"Police identified the deceased as 47-year-old Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu, an Indian national travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter. His body was taken to a hospital in Lukla.49-year-old Shailesh Krishna Patel, an Indian-origin resident of New Zealand, was also injured who was travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter. He was airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu by a Prabhu helicopter, police inspector Mausam Tamang said.The other two injured pilots were identified as Rabindra Prajapati of Fishtail Air and Prajwal KC of Air Dynasty.Both were taken to Kathmandu for further treatment.Three people were injured in the accident, including two pilots and a passenger.Police inspector Mausam Tamang identified the injured passenger as Shailesh Krishna Patel, a 49-year-old Indian-origin resident of New Zealand. He was travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter along with Balaramaramadu.Patel was airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu for treatment in a Prabhu helicopter, Tamang said.The two injured Nepali pilots were identified as Rabindra Prajapati of Fishtail Air and Prajwal KC of Air Dynasty. Both were taken to Kathmandu for further medical treatment.Fishtail Air said its helicopter was carrying tourists who had been rescued from the Everest region when it crashed while attempting to land. A company official confirmed that Balaramaramadu and Patel were among the passengers.The Air Dynasty helicopter, meanwhile, was carrying cargo, according to an official from the company.Solukhumbu chief district officer Kaman Singh Thapa Magar confirmed the collision to Reuters and said the injured New Zealand passenger had been rescued.Police have yet to confirm the total number of people aboard the two helicopters at the time of the accident.Pheriche is a settlement along the route to the Mount Everest base camp, around 150 km north-east of Kathmandu. It is an important stop for trekkers and climbers heading towards the world's highest mountain.The collision occurred during Nepal's peak trekking season, when helicopter services are widely used to ferry tourists, mountaineers and rescued trekkers across the Everest region.The exact cause of the collision remains unclear. Police said they were collecting further details about the incident.Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN) deputy spokesperson Gyanendra Bhul said that the helicopters were approaching the landing area from different directions when the accident occurred, BBC Nepali reported.According to Bhul, one helicopter was travelling from Lukla, while the other was returning from Gorakhpur, near the Everest base camp. Both reportedly attempted to land at the same spot."It appears that the accident occurred when helicopters travelling from Lukla and returning from Gorakhpur, near the base camp, tried to land at the same place," Bhul said.The exact cause of the collision remains unclear. However, preliminary information suggests that snow-covered helipads may have played a role in the accident."It looks like they tried to land on one of the other helipads, perhaps because it was covered in snow, even though there were other helipads," he said.The authorities have not yet released further details about the identities of those involved or the circumstances leading to the collision.
Article Summary: The two helicopters collided while attempting to land near Mount Everest in Nepal on Tuesday morning. One helicopter was travelling from Lukla, while the other was returning from Gorakhpur, near the Everest base camp. Both reportedly attempted to land at the same spot. An Indian national was killed and three others, including a New Zealand resident of Indian origin, were injured.

He scored one century and two half-centuries, with his highest score being 123 not out.Meanwhile, India captain Shubman Gill has confirmed the team's top four batters for the five-match ODI series against New Zealand.Gill said the top order would feature four right-handed batters - himself, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer. The team will follow a flexible approach for the No. 5 and No. 6 positions, with KL Rahul and Axar Patel available depending on the situation."We will have a floating approach for No. 5 and No.6. Our top four is set, all right-handers. So if lefty is needed, Axar bhai goes and depending on match situation even KL bhai can go. So bit flexible," Gill said at the pre-match press conference ahead of the first ODI.India will begin their five-match ODI series against New Zealand in Auckland on November 4.
Article Summary: Sachin Tendulkar is top of the list with 652 runs in 18 ODIs played in New Zealand. Virender Sehwag is second with 598 runs in 12 matches. Virat Kohli, who occupies the third position with 514 runs in 11 matches. India captain Shubman Gill has confirmed the team's top four batters for the five-match ODI series.

Article Title: Bengaluru man holds woman at knifepoint, threatens to kill her in full public view during gold chain snatching bid
Article Text:
In Bengaluru's Indiranagar, a woman named Jayashree was attacked while working at a shop

Locals overpower accused, rescue woman

Accused arrested, remanded to judicial custody





BENGALURU: A woman working at a shop in Bengaluru's Indiranagar was held at knifepoint, threatened with murder and had her hands stuck to a table with Fevikwik after a man barged into the shop and attempted to snatch her gold chain on October 31.Alert locals rushed to her rescue, overpowered the accused and handed him over to the police.The incident occurred around 11.45am in the Indiranagar police station limits. The accused, identified as Prabhuraj alias Raj, allegedly walked into the shop and initially pretended that someone was chasing him and trying to kill him, asking the woman to shelter him.However, he soon turned on her, allegedly pulling out a knife and holding it against her neck. He threatened her and demanded her gold chain, reportedly weighing 35 grams and valued at around Rs 4.5 lakh.In an attempt to prevent her from resisting or escaping, the accused allegedly poured Fevikwik on both her hands and stuck them to the shop table. He then attempted to take the chain from her neck.The woman screamed for help as the accused tried to snatch her chain. Hearing her cries, neighbouring shopkeepers and passersby rushed into the shop.Realising that he was surrounded, Prabhuraj held the knife against her neck and threatened to kill her if anyone came closer. He allegedly tried to use the woman as a shield to escape from the crowd.However, locals managed to divert his attention, overpower him and rescue the woman before handing him over to Indiranagar police.The woman was subsequently rescued and taken to hospital. She was reported to have escaped without serious injuries.Police registered a case at Indiranagar police station and arrested Prabhuraj. He was subsequently remanded to judicial custody.The accused reportedly worked as a delivery agent. Police are verifying his background and investigating the circumstances surrounding the attempted chain snatching.A video showing the accused threatening the woman and dragging her during the incident has since surfaced on social media, triggering concern over the safety of people working in shops.
Article Summary: A woman working at a shop in Bengaluru's Indiranagar was held at knifepoint, threatened with murder and had her hands stuck to a table with Fevikwik.Alert locals rushed to her rescue, overpowered the accused and handed him over to the police. He was subsequently remanded to judicial custody.

Article Title: Tusshar Kapoor gets Rs 5 crore extortion threat in name of Bishnoi gang; police suspect impersonator
Article Text:
Tusshar Kapoor received an extortion call demanding Rs 5 crore from someone posing as a gang member





MUMBAI: Bollywood actor Tusshar Kapoor allegedly received an extortion call demanding Rs 5 crore from a person claiming to be Harry Boxer, a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.However, a preliminary investigation by the Mumbai Crime Branch has ruled out the involvement of Bishnoi gang members in the threat call.Tusshar has informally alerted the Mumbai Police about the threat, following which his security has been beefed up. The investigation has been handed over to the Crime Branch and its Anti-Extortion Cell.According to police sources, the Crime Branch’s technical team examined the audio recording of the threatening call and compared the sender’s voice with official audio samples of Harry Boxer available in its database.The analysis reportedly found no match between the two recordings.Police suspect that an unidentified person may have impersonated a Bishnoi gang member and used the gang’s name to intimidate the actor and extort money.No First Information Report (FIR) has been registered so far, as the police are continuing their investigation to establish the origin of the audio recording and identify the caller.
Article Summary: Bollywood actor Tusshar Kapoor allegedly received an extortion call demanding Rs 5 crore from a person claiming to be Harry Boxer. A preliminary investigation by the Mumbai Crime Branch has ruled out the involvement of Bishnoi gang members in the threat call.

Article Title: ‘Mother-in-law responsible if anything happens to me’: Pune techie's last message before she was found hanging in flat; husband held
Article Text:
Payal Zambre Patil was found hanging in a flat in Mukund Nagar following conflicts with her mother-in-law.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that family disputes can lead to tragic outcomes? Yes, very much No, not usually 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PUNE: A 29-year-old woman, daughter-in-law of a prominent businessman in Pune, was found hanging from a ceiling fan in a flat in Mukund Nagar on Monday morning, following an alleged dispute with her mother-in-law.Police arrested her husband and registered a case of harassment and abetment of suicide against four members of her in-laws' family after her relatives accused them of subjecting her to harassment over repeated demands for gold.According to news agency PTI, the deceased, Payal Zambre Patil, was an IT professional before she quit her job.She was married to Akshay Zambre Patil, and the couple has a three-year-old daughter.Senior inspector Yashwant Nikam of Swargate police station said Payal lived with her in-laws in Mukund Nagar, off Pune-Satara Road. On Monday morning, she allegedly sent messages to some people stating that her mother-in-law would be responsible if anything happened to her.Police said Payal had an argument with her mother-in-law on Sunday and left her matrimonial home. Her family and in-laws began searching for her on Monday morning.She was eventually found hanging from a ceiling fan in another flat in an apartment complex near their residence. The incident came to light around 11.30am."When police reached the apartment, she was found hanging from the ceiling. No suicide note was found," a Swargate police station official said, adding that statements of her maternal relatives were being recorded.Payal's brother, Rishikesh Pawar, alleged that her husband and in-laws appeared unconcerned when he reached their home on Monday morning. He claimed they began searching for her only after the family questioned them.According to Pawar, the in-laws returned within five minutes and informed them that Payal was in a nearby apartment. He alleged that the flat's door was locked from inside and he managed to enter through the rear balcony, where he found his sister hanging.He further claimed that Payal had repeatedly complained about harassment by her mother-in-law. Recalling Sunday's argument, Pawar said he had called Akshay and told him that the dispute was temporary and could be resolved.Payal's uncle alleged that she had been harassed over demands for gold since her marriage. He claimed her in-laws demanded 10 tolas of gold every Diwali."This year too, they demanded gold, but we told them that we were farmers and, given the drought-like situation, it was not possible for us to meet the demand. We had even promised to give the gold next year," he alleged.The complaint filed by Payal's family also accused her husband and in-laws of mentally harassing her during her pregnancy in 2022 by pressuring her to give birth to a boy. After she delivered a girl on March 30, 2023, her in-laws allegedly argued with her at the hospital and said they would not take responsibility for either her or the child, the complaint stated.Following her death, relatives from Payal's parental family allegedly vandalised her in-laws' residence, office and marriage hall, triggering tension in the area. Her father-in-law owns a marriage hall and an eatery on Pune-Satara Road, police said. Her parental family runs a business in the Khed-Shivapur area.Swargate police registered a case of harassment and abetment of suicide against four people, including Payal's husband and mother-in-law. Senior inspector Nikam said Akshay had been arrested and two police teams were formed to trace the remaining accused.While Payal's family has alleged that she was murdered and her death staged as suicide, police have registered a case of abetment of suicide. The circumstances surrounding her death are being investigated.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Payal Zambre Patil, 29, was found hanging from a ceiling fan in a flat in Mukund Nagar on Monday morning. Police arrested her husband and registered a case of harassment and abetment of suicide against four members of her in-laws' family. Her relatives accused them of subjecting her to harassment over demands for gold.

Article Title: Major fire breaks out at HPCL Visakhapatnam refinery, no casualties
Article Text:
A fire occurred at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited Visakh Refinery during the night, alarming nearby residents.





VISAKHAPATNAM: A fire that broke out at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's (HPCL) Visakhapatnam refinery in Malkapuram on Monday night was brought under control, with no casualties or injuries reported.The fire was confined to a pitch intermediate storage tank in the refinery's sulfur unit, and all units at the facility are operating safely, HPCL said.In a post on X, the company said the fire was reported around 10pm on November 2, following which its Fire and Safety Team immediately activated firefighting and emergency response measures."The fire was localised to the pitch tank area and was brought under control within a short time. There have been no casualties," HPCL said, adding that all refinery units were functioning safely.Malkapuram Circle Inspector E Narasimha Rao said the fire involved sulfur pitch, a waste or bottom product generated in the refinery's sulfur unit. He said HPCL's own fire tenders were deployed to tackle the blaze and no external assistance was required."There are no casualties, no injuries and no major issues. Everyone is safe, and there is no need for panic," he said.Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) Dileep Chakravarthy, who visited the site, said the fire had been completely extinguished using the firefighting equipment installed at the refinery and resources deployed by the Andhra Pradesh Fire Department.He said a small blast was reported at the facility before the fire broke out. Chakravarthy added that an enquiry would be initiated to examine industrial safety at the facility in accordance with applicable norms."There is no cause for worry, and no injuries or casualties have been reported. People are requested not to panic about the incident," he said.Meanwhile, eyewitnesses said the flames rising from the refinery were large enough to frighten people in the vicinity. One eyewitness said people moved away from the area after seeing the blaze.
Article Summary: A fire broke out at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's (HPCL) Visakhapatnam refinery on Monday night. No casualties or injuries were reported. The fire was confined to a pitch intermediate storage tank in the refinery's sulfur unit.

Article Title: Dilip Ghosh takes 'Sonia' jibe at Mamata for joining INDIA bloc rally against SIR
Article Text:
Ghosh claimed that Banerjee's party has lost political ground in its state and that she was seeking political relevance by aligning with the Congress leadership.

Festive season security arrangements

Ghosh targets Mamata over development boards

NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh on Tuesday criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Taking a dig at Mamata, he said that she was turning to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi for leadership out of "utter helplessness".Ghosh claimed that Banerjee's party has lost political ground in its state and that she was seeking political relevance by aligning with the Congress leadership.“Earlier, she set out to become the top leader herself. Now, she has nothing left in her hands. Today, she isn’t even an elected representative. That is why, out of utter helplessness, she goes around accepting Sonia ji as her leader again. Her party is finished today,” news agency ANI reported, quoting Ghosh.He also hit out at Banerjee over her objections to the electoral process, saying political parties must respect the people's mandate. He alleged that she had no complaints about the Election Commission or democracy when her party was winning elections.“As long as she was winning, democracy was fine, and the Election Commission was fine. The moment she lost, everything went wrong. Keep faith in the people; the people decide who wins and who loses. One must accept the verdict of the public,” he said.The minister further claimed that the removal of fake voters during the electoral roll revision had paved the way for free and fair elections in West Bengal. He alleged that Banerjee had benefited from such voters in previous elections.“Look, when the revision occurred, the fake voter base through which Mamata used to win was eliminated. Once they were separated, a free and fair election took place. A genuine election happened in Bengal after many years, and people are happy about it; change has arrived. No outsider can simply enter and become a citizen of this country or avail benefits here,” he said.Ghosh also said the ruling government and party workers would organise rallies across the state to counter the Opposition's attempts to create unrest and communicate their position to the public.“It is also our responsibility to make people understand and deliver the right message. The people are nationalist, and the government is nationalist. No one will be permitted to create unrest in the country. We will also reach out to the people and hold rallies everywhere; this is just the beginning,” he said.Meanwhile, Ghosh said the state government was making arrangements to ensure that Deepavali, Kali Puja and Jagaddhatri Puja celebrations passed off peacefully.He said every cabinet minister had been assigned a district to oversee law and order during the festive season. Ghosh has been given responsibility for Purba Medinipur, also known as East Midnapore.“The government is keeping a close watch across all of West Bengal to ensure that the upcoming Deepavali, Kali Puja, and Jagaddhatri Puja are conducted smoothly and with enthusiasm. Every cabinet minister has been assigned the responsibility of overseeing law and order in one district. I have been given charge of Purba Medinipur (East Midnapore). I am also meeting with them to ensure all arrangements are in place and nothing goes wrong. This is the government’s duty, and the public must cooperate,” he said.The minister also criticised the previous Trinamool Congress government over the functioning of development boards set up for marginalised communities, including the Matua community.He alleged that several boards formed during Banerjee's tenure had not received adequate funds or been given meaningful work.“Mamata Banerjee had formed several development boards in West Bengal: the Rajbanshi Board, the Matua Board, the Bhumij Adivasi Board, but gave neither funds nor work to anyone. She only played politics,” he said.Ghosh said the Matua community, many of whose members migrated from Bangladesh, continued to face economic hardships and needed focused development measures. He said the board should be made functional and provided with funds.“Now, for that community, especially the Matua community, most of whom came from Bangladesh, have numerous hardships and are poor. Their development must happen; therefore, the board must be actively functional for them, and funds must be provided, which our chief minister (Suvendu Adhikari) has initiated," he said.
Article Summary: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Ghosh claimed that Banerée's party has lost political ground in its state and that she was seeking political relevance by aligning with the Congress leadership.

Article Title: 'Air fares up by 700%': Don't fly, says SC
Article Text:
SC refuses urgent hearing on plea against steep rise in domestic airfares ahead of Diwali

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday refused to urgently list a plea against steep rise in domestic air fares during Diwali season and seeking a direction to Centre to frame a mechanism to cap air fares on domestic routes during festival periods.The issue of regulation of air fares is still pending before SC, a bench hearing the plea was informed while seeking the court's intervention. But the court turned down the plea.Advocate Abhinav for the petitioner submitted that fares have gone up 700% amounts to a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution. "Don't travel by air," the bench said.Centre had earlier told SC that the rules on air fares under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, will be published in two weeks.
Article Summary: Supreme Court refuses to urgently list a plea against steep rise in domestic air fares during Diwali season. The issue of regulation of air fares is still pending before SC. Centre had earlier told SC that the rules on air fares under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam will be published in two weeks.

Article Title: Navy rescues 20 crew members of fishing vessel from armed pirates over 3,000km from Mumbai, Rajnath praises 48-hr op
Article Text:
Navy rescues all 20 crew members of fishing vessel Azini from armed pirates in a 48-hour operation in the Arabian Sea, with support from the Indian Air Force

NEW DELHI: The Indian Navy has rescued all 20 crew members of a fishing vessel from armed pirates after a 48-hour operation in the Arabian Sea. The vessel, Azini, was reportedly seized by the armed pirates more than 3,000 km from Mumbai.Defence minister Rajnath Singh praised the Indian Navy for executing the meticulously coordinated 48-hour operation with support from the Indian Air Force. “The swift localisation, interception and safe release of the crew and vessel from significantly-armed pirates, with timely support from the IAF, speak well of the Indian Navy’s high operational readiness and ability to respond decisively to maritime threats across the region,” Rajnath said.A photograph shared by the minister on his post on X shows destroyer INS Kolkata standing by as heavily armed commandos guard what appear to be the pirates, seated on the deck of the fishing vessel. A huge cache of seized weapons was also seen lying on the vessel.“Our brave personnel have once again demonstrated India’s ability, intent and resolve to safeguard lives, uphold maritime security and ensure stability across the Indian Ocean Region.India continues to stand resolute in ensuring SAFE SEAS and a free, open and secure IOR,” he said.Monday’s operation was launched much further than the Navy's landmark anti-piracy mission of March 2024. The same destroyer had then intercepted the pirate ship MV Ruen around 2,600km from the Indian coast.The Indian Navy has deployed over 10 warships for anti-piracy and regional security operations like Operation Sankalp to patrol the Arabian Sea, Gulf of Aden, and the East Coast of Africa.Indian Navy has been proactively engaging with the regional and extra-regional navies and maritime forces, to promote maritime security. Article Title: Unhappy with Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, six NCP biggies meet Amit Shah
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah met senior NCP leaders at his residence amid growing concerns over internal differences in the party following Ajit Pawar's death

NCP leaders Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Chhagan Bhujbal and others attended a meeting with Amit Shah in Delhi, amid reports of discontent over Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth's leadership

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI/PUNE: With BJP concerned over organisational discord within NCP, home minister Amit Shah late Sunday met senior functionaries believed to be unhappy with party president Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, and nudged them to resolve their internal rift in the interest of the party.The meeting was attended by NCP national working president Praful Patel, Maharashtra chief Sunil Tatkare, ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, and netas Dhananjay Munde and Dilip Patil. Neither deputy CM Sunetra nor Parth was present. Sunetra then called a core committee meet in Mumbai.Sources said the dissidents' concerns remained unresolved after talks with Sunetra, Parth and his younger sibling Jay. Days ahead will prove crucial for NCP, which is a part of the BJP-led NDA.The rift has been brewing over what confidants of late Ajit Pawar see as Parth's attempt to push important decisions through his mother without consulting them. Ajit's sudden death in a plane crash had thrust Sunetra into the leadership. The immediate trigger appeared to be NCP's loss in the lone MLC seat it contested. The Sharad Pawar-led faction won two seats, suggesting some family loyalists may have returned to veteran's camp.At the meeting with Shah, the group aired grievances, particularly about Parth allegedly riding roughshod over the party, with his mother allowing him to have his way.NCP seniors, who sided with Ajit during the split with Sharad Pawar, did not criticise Sunetra. However, they resented her allowing Parth to repeatedly call the shots, suggesting she backed him, an unhappy party member said. "Having grown in a political family and married into Pawar clan, she has enough smarts not to sense the unease among seniors," he said.Ajit's confidants at Shah's residence underlined Sunetra and Parth's isolation.BJP believes organisational discord in NCP could help opposition, especially NCP-SP, regain ground in western Maharashtra and hurt the governing coalition. Shinde-led Shiv Sena is its third partner. Shinde, a Maratha like Pawars, could use NCP's decline to gain leverage over BJP.Merger talks between two NCP factions were also raised at Shah's residence, sources said. Tatkare rejected suggestions that discussions continued. "The curtains have drawn on merger issue. Even seniors of the other NCP faction have said so," he said after the core committee meeting. Hours earlier, NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule had attended INDIA bloc rally in Delhi.Tatkare claimed there were no differences in the party. But functionaries held another meeting at Bhujbal's Mumbai residence, again without Sunetra or Parth. Chief spokesperson Umesh Patil said attempts were being made to give "unnecessary political colour" to Shah's meeting and create a false narrative of internal differences.
Article Summary: NCP leaders Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Chhagan Bhujbal and others attended a meeting with Amit Shah in Delhi, amid reports of discontent over Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth's leadership. Days ahead will prove crucial for NCP, which is a part of the BJP-led NDA.

Article Title: Row erupts after Scottish govt sends IT contract to Bengaluru to administer welfare payment
Article Text:
Scotland’s SNP government faces criticism for awarding a £35.4 million contract to Bengaluru-based Mphasis to manage its welfare benefits platform, which serves around two million citizens

TOI correspondent from London:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Scottish National Party, which governs Scotland, has come under fire from opposition ministers for handing a £35.4 million (almost Rs 450 crore) contract to an IT services company in Bengaluru.Under the contract, Mphasis will manage and maintain Scotland’s benefits management platform that delivers welfare benefits to around two million citizens across Scotland.Scotland first minister John Swinney has just returned from a trade mission to India where he was meant to be finding opportunities to support jobs and prosperity across Scotland, so news that he has instead sent lucrative work to India has sparked fiery criticism back home.Scottish Labour’s social justice spokesman, Mark Griffin, told the “Scottish Mail on Sunday”: “We should be using public contracts like this to boost local business and the Scottish economy and create jobs in Scotland. All too often, under SNP, good work has flowed overseas. SNP ministers should explain why this decision was made.”Shadow secretary of state for Scotland Harriet Cross posted on X: “They send millions to India to help administer their ballooning benefits system.This is taxpayers’ money. And they’re sending it abroad.”“Our ongoing relationship with Social Security Scotland allows us to support one of the country’s most critical public service platforms, and our commitment is to maintain continuity, improve operational efficiency and deliver meaningful outcomes for individuals and families across Scotland. The project aligns with our broader public sector focus; supporting govt organisations in running secure, reliable and future-ready digital services,” said Ashish Devalekar, executive vice-president and head of Europe, Mphasis.A Social Security Scotland spokesperson told TOI: “Contracts are awarded in line with the Scottish govt’s procurement guidelines, which state that bids are to be treated equally, regardless of the location. This ensures that we award contracts to the bidder offering the best overall value. Investment in technology ensures we are future proof and adaptable to changing demands for our payments.”Sources in the Scottish govt told TOI that the platform “requires highly specialised expertise in a niche technology area with a relatively small number of suppliers globally able to demonstrate the scale, experience and capability required”.
Article Summary: Scotland’s SNP government faces criticism for awarding a £35.4 million contract to Bengaluru-based Mphasis. Under the contract, Mphasis will manage and maintain Scotland's benefits management platform that delivers welfare benefits to around two million citizens. Scotland first minister John Swinney has just returned from a trade mission to India.

Article Title: SC orders trial in Ram temple donation case; SIT says Rs 2.7 crore stolen
Article Text:
SC clears trial of eight accused of siphoning Rs 2.7 crore in Ayodhya Ram temple donations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Five months after news broke of pilferage of donations at Ayodhya Ram temple, Supreme Court cleared trial of eight people, who figure in the chargesheet filed by the SIT for allegedly siphoning Rs 2.7 crore. It also gave the petitioners, who had sought probe, the status of victims of crime and allowed them to assist in the trial, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.The SIT's status report informed SC that financial and forensic examination extended to cash deposits, transactions, property purchases, construction expenditure, vehicles, jewellery, other assets, and event-related spendings. "The amount of alleged embezzlement is approximately Rs 2.7 crore," the report said.On Monday, solicitor general Tushar Mehta explained to the court the process that involved scrutiny of bank accounts and acquisition of immoveable properties by the accused, as well as examination of CCTV footage that culminated in the chargesheet Sept 23.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the trial court to proceed with the trial in accordance with law. On the large number of petitioners who had sought an independent probe into the donation theft, the bench said the petitioners can be given the status of victims of crime, and in public interest, they can assist the prosecutor and trial court in proceedings.One of the petitioners also sought a direction from SC for an “independent, impartial, technically competent survey/demarcation” of the land that was allotted for the temple by SC in its Nov 9, 2019, judgement.He also sought a direction to the revenue and statutory authorities to place before SC relevant records and their comparison with the site plan and actual location of the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple complex to determine if the present complex stands on the land allotted by the court.While Mehta said it is impermissible for the petitioner to seek a virtual reopening of the judgement by a fivejudge bench, the bench said if the petitioner had any grievance about the demarcation of the land, he should approach the civil court with a civil suit.
Article Summary: Supreme Court clears trial of eight accused of siphoning Rs 2.7 crore in Ayodhya Ram temple donations. It also gave the petitioners, who had sought probe, the status of victims of crime and allowed them to assist in the trial.

Article Title: Day after quitting as Punjab MLAs, 3 AAP rebels come into BJP fold
Article Text:
Three former AAP MLAs from Punjab join BJP a day after resigning, citing concerns over rising crime, drugs and gangsterism in the poll-bound state

NEW DELHI: A day after resigning as MLAs in Punjab, three AAP members joined BJP here on Monday, giving a boost to the saffron outfit in the poll-bound state.BJP is making an all-out push to emerge as a serious contender for office in the state after languishing on the margins so far.Chetan Singh Jouramajra, a former cabinet minister elected from Samana, former IPS officer Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, who won from Amritsar North, and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, who represented Sanaur in the assembly, decried "rising" gangsterism and drug abuse in the state and expressed confidence in BJP's ability to turn things around as they joined the party.In his remarks, Vijay Pratap Singh said, "Crime, drugs, corruption and gangsterism are rampant in Punjab. Bhagwant Mann and Arvind Kejriwal have completely uprooted and destroyed AAP, which was born from a revolutionary mindset."
Article Summary: Three former AAP MLAs from Punjab join BJP a day after resigning. They cited concerns over rising crime, drugs and gangsterism in the state. BJP is making an all-out push to emerge as a serious contender for office in Punjab.

Article Title: SC on Diwali: Crackers on Nov 7-8 in 2 time slots, and keep it green

SC allows green crackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8 during specified hours

NEW DELHI: Holding that Deepawali has a religious, social, psychological and emotional significance for people, Supreme Court on Monday kept the window open for bursting of green firecrackers on Nov 7 and 8 between 6am and 7am, and between 8pm and 10pm.The court had allowed bursting of crackers at the same time last year too.A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale directed police and administration to ensure polluting crackers remain out of bounds for people in Delhi, and take punitive action against those who deal in such crackers.While acknowledging Deepawali's significance, the court stressed that the right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, was only a qualified one and not exempt from restrictions allowed by the Constitution."...Allowing the environment to degrade, which results in a health hazard to all living beings, defeats the very purpose of the festivities... All parties before us are ad idem (of one mind) on the fact that bursting of firecrackers is contributing enormously to pollution in Delhi/NCR," it said. Restriction on manufacture and sale of crackers in the national capital will continue after Diwali.The bench, however, did not favour a complete ban on firecrackers.“Though imposition of a blanket ban seems to be the ideal solution, we are of the opinion that this court, at this point in time, is short of adequate data to decide whether or not a complete ban would be the best solution to solve the problem of environmental pollution, caused by bursting firecrackers,” it said.The bench directed district collectors/commissioners, in consultation with the superintendent of police concerned, to identify and designate locations in the NCR to facilitate the sale of green crackers and banned online sale. “The sale of firecrackers shall be strictly prohibited in any other location, other than the designated ones, including sale through online platforms,” it said.“We direct the authorities concerned to mandate all manufacturers and traders of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR to furnish a monetary security, which shall be a handsome amount, as determined by them. The said security deposit shall immediately stand forfeited in case any manufacturer or trader of firecrackers violates any of the directions passed by this court,” the bench said.The court noted in its order that bursting of firecrackers, though constituting a religious practice meant to celebrate the occasion, would result in severe environmental pollution, especially air and noise, apart from the creation of solid waste. It said the unregulated practice affected everyone, including the end user and, among human beings, children, disabled and elderly people constituted the most vulnerable groups.“It is not in dispute that the right to practice, profess and propagate religion conferred under Article 25(1) of the Constitution is certainly subject to public order, morality, health and other provisions of Part III of the Constitution. This court has repeatedly held that ‘right to life’ envisaged under Article 21 of the Constitution includes the right to a healthy, safe and pollution-free environment, and the said position has been crystallised and, hence, requires no repetition.Therefore, the right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, is only a qualified one and cannot go beyond constitutional restrictions,” the bench said.It added that there shall be no manufacture or sale of firecrackers joined in series (‘ladis’) and garlands. Use of firecrackers with barium and those not approved by CSIRNEERI as green crackers shall not be permitted.
Article Summary: SC allows green crackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8 during specified hours. Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale directed police and administration to ensure polluting crackers remain out of bounds. Restriction on manufacture and sale of crackers will continue after Diwali.

Article Title: Cyclone Murasu crosses Andhra coast, gale winds up to 120 kmph - top developments
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu made landfall along the south Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole early Tuesday, with its eye entering the coast and a major part of its wall cloud moving over land, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. The landfall point is between Nellore and Narsapur.Gale winds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, are likely along and off the coast during landfall and are expected to persist. The IMD has also forecast heavy rainfall over the next 12 hours and a storm surge of 1-1.5 metres above the astronomical tide, which could inundate low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh.Heavy rainfall has already lashed parts of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, while Odisha has stepped up preparedness amid concerns over fresh damage following Cyclone Arnab.The IMD has warned that a storm surge of 1-1.5 metres above the astronomical tide could inundate low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh until the morning of November 3. Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts are likely to experience the maximum surge before it gradually decreases.Heavy spells of rainfall are also expected along the south Andhra coast over the next 12 hours.Gale winds of 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph, are likely to continue along and off the coast until morning, the weather department said.Andhra Pradesh government rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu.Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a "Hi" to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the "Services" option from the menu. Choose "Murasu Cyclone Issues". Click on "Report Issue" and confirm.Select "Registration" and enter essential details, including name, district, and mandal.At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled across Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati airports as the cyclone approached the Andhra Pradesh coast.Vijayawada Airport director M Lakshmi Kantha Reddy said IndiGo cancelled 10 flights and Air India Express two. Four flights were cancelled at Visakhapatnam airport, while three were cancelled at Tirupati airport.Chennai airport authorities also cancelled some flights and advised passengers to contact their respective airlines for updates.Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to remain on alert as moderate to heavy rainfall and strong winds were expected across south coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema.Naidu expressed hope that the impact would be limited, citing forecasts of lower wind speeds and rainfall intensity compared with Cyclone Arnab.The state energy department also placed power utilities on high alert, directing officials to take precautionary measures to minimise damage to electricity infrastructure and ensure uninterrupted power supply.Energy minister G Ravi Kumar asked distribution companies to remain particularly vigilant in the vulnerable regions.Tamil Nadu extended assistance to its neighbouring state, deploying three National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams comprising 90 personnel and 25 electricity department teams with 500 personnel and essential equipment.Karnataka also announced that it would send 500 skilled power personnel along with equipment to help restore electricity infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Arnab.Heavy rainfall also lashed several parts of Chennai, Chengalpattu and Tiruvallur districts, with showers continuing since Sunday night.The weather department warned of very heavy rainfall in Chennai and Tiruvallur, while heavy showers were forecast for Chengalpattu, Kanchipuram, Ranipet, Vellore and the Nilgiris.Schools in Chennai were closed on Monday as authorities braced for further rainfall. The IMD said rain intensity was likely to ease only after the cyclone completely crossed the coast.Odisha stepped up evacuation efforts in vulnerable areas as the cyclone was expected to bring heavy rainfall to its southern districts, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri.Disaster management minister Suresh Pujari said district collectors had been alerted and more than 300 rescue teams from the NDRF, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) and fire services had been kept on standby.Schools and colleges in some southern districts have been closed until November 3.The fresh weather threat has also raised concerns over the ongoing search for 10 people missing in a landslide.The approaching cyclone has added to the concerns of farmers whose standing crops were damaged by Cyclone Arnab and subsequent flooding.Ganjam district reported the maximum damage to paddy crops, with several fields inundated. Farmers fear another spell of heavy rainfall could cause further losses and damage crops nearing harvest.Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil said Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods had affected 1.18 lakh people, damaged 1,672 houses and impacted 75,388 hectares of agricultural land.The agriculture department, however, estimated the damaged crop area at around 90,000 hectares.Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced a special relief package for those affected by Cyclone Arnab, adding that it would be reviewed after an assessment of the damage caused by Murasu.
Article Summary: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu made landfall along the south Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole early Tuesday. At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled across Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati airports. The IMD has warned that a storm surge of 1-1.5 metres above the astronomical tide could inundate low-lying areas.

Article Title: 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 UP elections?
Article Text:
The SP chief’s public show of support for the veteran leader comes amid questions over the Azam Khan family’s influence on the party’s prospects ahead of the 2027 elections.

Azam the, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge"

Azam was, Azam is and Azam will remain

The brief freedom

Azam Khan’s rise in SP was closely tied to his long-standing association with Mulayam Singh Yadav.

Akhilesh turns arrest into political battle

The Muslim vote and the Owaisi challenge

Muslims account for at least 30% of the population in around 70 constituencies.

Owaisi has attacked Akhilesh Yadav over the treatment of Azam Khan's family.

From kingmaker to political liability?

BJP's counter: 'Mafia raj' and law and order

UP accused Akhilesh of opposing Azam Khan’s release out of concern that the veteran leader could challenge his position in party.
