NEW DELHI: ").With that emphatic declaration, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav sought to end speculation about his equation with one of the party's tallest Muslim leaders. But the political reality surrounding Mohammad Azam Khan is far more complicated than the slogan suggests.Nine days after Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam at Rampur jail, the veteran leader walked out of prison with his son Abdullah Azam after the Allahabad high court granted them bail in the dual PAN card case. His freedom, however, lasted barely minutes. The Enforcement Directorate arrested him in a separate money-laundering case linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, and a court subsequently remanded him to 14 days' judicial custody.The dramatic turn has put Akhilesh's declaration to the test. Once among the most powerful figures in the SP, Azam remains central to the party's political calculations in Rampur and its relationship with Muslim voters. But his legal battles, the erosion of his family's electoral stronghold and the growing challenge from Asaduddin Owaisi have turned his return into a complicated political proposition.As Uttar Pradesh heads towards the 2027 assembly election, Akhilesh faces a question that goes beyond personal loyalty: can he hold on to Azam's political legacy without becoming hostage to its baggage?Azam and Abdullah had been in custody since November 2025 following their conviction in the dual PAN card case.The Allahabad high court's order suspended their 10-year sentences and granted them bail, paving the way for their release.However, the ED had a separate case waiting. The agency arrested Azam shortly after he walked out of Rampur jail, while Abdullah was allowed to go home.The money-laundering investigation relates to alleged financial irregularities in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. The ED has alleged that government funds were diverted for the university's construction. Azam is the founder of the university and heads the trust that runs it. These are allegations being investigated by the agency, not findings of guilt in the present case.Speaking to reporters after his release, Azam alleged that he was being punished for being a Muslim and for establishing a university and schools. "What is there left to say? What can I say? The law has ceased to exist. Is this the punishment for being a Muslim?" he said.The following day, a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad sent him to 14 days' judicial custody. The court proceedings ensured that the brief release did not translate into a return to political activity.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav responded sharply to the ED action, accusing the BJP government of using cases to repeatedly send an elderly political leader to jail.In a post on X, the SP chief said: "Let today's rulers remember that thrones change when the time changes. The conspiracy being hatched against Mr Azam Khan through these cases is being watched not just by the entire country, but by the whole world."He added that repeatedly implicating an elderly man in cases and sending him to jail was "an utterly cowardly act", warning that injustice could eventually turn into a calamity for those responsible.The response was significant because it came barely nine days after Akhilesh had visited Azam in jail. That meeting had already signalled that the SP chief was unwilling to distance himself from the veteran leader despite the legal controversies surrounding him.The ED arrest has now sharpened the political messaging. For Akhilesh, the issue is no longer simply Azam's return to the party's political fold. It is also about positioning the SP against what it describes as the misuse of investigative agencies to target opposition leaders.The BJP, on the other hand, has defended the ED action, maintaining that the law applies equally to everyone.For the Samajwadi Party, the stakes in the Azam Khan question go well beyond the fortunes of one leader. They concern the party's hold over a crucial section of its traditional support base: Muslim voters. Muslims account for roughly 19% of Uttar Pradesh's population, making them one of the state's largest voting blocs. Their concentration in several constituencies gives them considerable electoral influence. In the 2022 assembly election, the community was a decisive factor in around 70 constituencies where Muslims formed at least 30% of the population.The 2022 results also showed how strongly the community rallied behind the SP. The party fielded 64 Muslim candidates, of whom 31 won, taking the total number of Muslim MLAs in the assembly to 36, up from 24 in 2017. The BSP fielded 88 Muslim candidates and the Congress 75, while AIMIM fielded more than 60. Yet neither the BSP nor Congress managed to elect a single Muslim MLA. The results suggested that the SP had emerged as the principal beneficiary of Muslim consolidation, even as smaller parties remained relevant in individual constituencies.Azam Khan was central to this political equation. His influence in Rampur and his standing among sections of the Muslim community gave the SP an important local and regional network. His electoral record, along with that of his wife Tazeen Fatima and son Abdullah Azam, made the family one of the most prominent Muslim political establishments in the state. His absence from active politics has therefore left a space that other political players may seek to occupy.It is this space that AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi is attempting to enter. His October 18 rally in Tanda was a reminder that the SP cannot take Muslim support for granted. Owaisi accused Akhilesh of treating Muslims as a vote bank while prioritising the Yadav community, and questioned why the SP leadership had not done more for Azam Khan. His pitch was for independent Muslim political representation, arguing that the community should produce its own MLAs and MPs rather than remain a support base for established political families.Owaisi's intervention is significant because the SP's electoral arithmetic depends not just on retaining Muslim support but also on preventing its fragmentation. The 2022 results showed the limits of smaller parties: although BSP and AIMIM fielded substantial numbers of Muslim candidates, neither managed to convert that presence into Muslim representation in the Assembly. However, even without winning seats, such parties can potentially affect the outcome in closely contested constituencies by splitting votes.Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam in Rampur jail was therefore also a political signal. His declaration, "Azam they, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge" (Azam was, is and will remain), aimed to reassure the veteran leader's followers that the SP had not abandoned him. The visit came amid growing questions over whether Owaisi could use sympathy for Azam to make inroads among Muslim voters.The challenge is compounded by the SP's wider social coalition strategy. Akhilesh has sought to move beyond the traditional Muslim-Yadav combination through his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework, bringing backward classes, Dalits and minorities under a broader political umbrella. But the party cannot afford to lose its Muslim support base while attempting to expand its reach among other communities.As the 2027 assembly election approaches, Akhilesh faces a delicate balancing act. He must reassure Azam's supporters that the SP continues to value the veteran leader and his political legacy, while ensuring that the party's Muslim support base does not become an opening for Owaisi or other rivals. The 2022 election demonstrated the electoral value of Muslim consolidation behind the SP. The question now is whether Akhilesh can hold that coalition together without relying too heavily on one leader or one political family.To understand Akhilesh Yadav's dilemma, one must first understand the extent of Azam Khan's influence in Rampur. For decades, Khan was not just the Samajwadi Party's most powerful face in the district but the man who dominated its political landscape. He challenged the influence of Rampur's erstwhile Nawab family and gradually built a formidable political network, winning the Rampur Sadar assembly seat 10 times. His influence extended beyond his own electoral victories: his wife, Tazeen Fatima, succeeded him as MLA in a 2019 bypoll, while his son Abdullah Azam twice won the Suar assembly seat. The Azam family's political presence became so entrenched that Rampur's electoral fortunes were often seen through the prism of Khan's influence.That hold was not easily broken. In the 2022 assembly election, Azam Khan won Rampur Sadar for the 10th time despite campaigning from jail. The BJP's Akash Saxena, one of his most prominent political adversaries who had pursued several cases against Azam Khan and his family, lost that contest. But the equation changed after Khan was disqualified following his conviction in a hate speech case. In the December 2022 bypoll, Saxena defeated Azam Khan's close aide Asim Raza by around 34,000 votes, delivering the BJP its first victory in Rampur Sadar and making Saxena the first Hindu candidate to win the constituency. The result marked a significant breach in a political stronghold that Khan and his family had dominated for decades.The erosion of the Azam family's influence became more apparent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. With Khan, his wife and son facing imprisonment, the SP fielded Maulana Mohibullah Nadvi from Rampur. The choice reportedly upset Khan's loyalists, many of whom stayed away from campaigning, exposing a growing rift between the local Azam camp and the party leadership. It was a reminder that Azam Khan's network could still matter to the SP even in his absence, but also that Akhilesh could no longer assume the family would automatically fall in line with the party's decisions.His treatment by the central agencies gives the party an opportunity to frame the issue as one of political targeting and due process. But the party will have to contend with the electoral consequences of being closely associated with a leader whose legal record has become a recurring political flashpoint.The challenge for Akhilesh is to retain the political value of the Azam network without allowing the controversies surrounding Khan and his family to define the SP's wider campaign. In Rampur, the question is no longer simply whether Azam Khan can return to politics. It is whether the political machinery he built can still deliver for the Samajwadi Party, and on whose terms.In 2022, UP CM Yogi Adityanath famously said: "Even Akhilesh doesn’t want Azam Khan to come out of jail because it will pose a threat to his position [chair]. The state government has nothing to do with these cases, whether they are related to Azam Khan or anyone else. It is the court that grants bail.""Under previous governments, mafias were running a parallel administration. When we took action against the land mafia who grabbed poor farmers' land for private universities and personal fiefdoms, the Samajwadi Party developed sympathy for criminals instead of the victims," he had said.The above remarks are at the core of the BJP's attack.The BJP has consistently used the Azam Khan issue to attack the Samajwadi Party's record on law and order. The party's broader political narrative has sought to associate the SP's previous tenure with alleged criminal influence and what it describes as 'mafia raj'.That gives the BJP an obvious line of attack if Akhilesh makes Azam's rehabilitation a central political theme. The ruling party can frame the SP's outreach as evidence that it has not moved away from its past.The SP, meanwhile, has to navigate the distinction between allegations, court findings and the political narrative built around them. It can point to the legal process and the need for due process, but it cannot wish away the electoral impact of the cases and convictions.The BJP's attack also puts the SP's broader coalition strategy under pressure. Akhilesh has sought to expand the party's social base beyond its traditional support groups through the PDA framework. A campaign dominated by the Azam Khan controversy could complicate that effort.Akhilesh's jail visit, his response to the ED arrest and the party's continued engagement with Azam Khan send a message to the SP's traditional supporters: the party has not abandoned a leader who played a major role in building its political presence.But the message also carries risks. The SP has to decide how much political space to give the Azam family, how prominently to project its association with them and how to prevent the issue from becoming a defining feature of its 2027 campaign.For Akhilesh, the Azam question will ultimately be about the political arithmetic as much as loyalty. He needs to reassure sections of the Muslim electorate that the SP remains attentive to their concerns, while keeping the PDA coalition broad enough to bring together backward classes, Dalits and minorities.As Uttar Pradesh moves towards 2027, Akhilesh's tightrope walk will be to retain the political value of an old ally without inheriting all the baggage that comes with him. Azam may be an asset the SP cannot easily discard, but he may also turn out to be a liability the party cannot afford to let define its next election.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's public show of support for the veteran leader comes amid questions over the Azam Khan family's influence on the party's prospects ahead of the 2027 elections. Azam's rise in SP was closely tied to his long-standing association with Mulayam Singh Yadav. His legal battles, the erosion of his family's electoral stronghold and the growing challenge from Asaduddin Owaisi have turned his return into a political proposition.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday responded sharply to a plea highlighting a steep surge in airfares, with Justice Vikram Nath telling the counsel, “Don’t travel by air. Next case,” before moving on to the next matter.The remark came after the counsel mentioned the plea before the court, claiming that airfares had increased by as much as 700 per cent. Arguing that air travel was an essential service, the counsel said the steep rise in ticket prices amounted to a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution, which guarantees equality before the law.“The airfares have increased to 700%. It is an essential service. Violation of Article 14,” the counsel submitted, according to Live Law.Justice Nath responded, “Don’t travel by air. Next case.”The court did not take up the plea at that stage and proceeded to the next matter. No order was passed on the submission.Meanwhile, India has adopted new airfare rules where government will not interfere in the process except “in an extraordinary situation (where) it considers it necessary to do so in the public interest.” Notified under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, which will be applicable from Jan 1, 2027, government has continued its policy of letting market forces determine airfares without government interference.TOI reported on Oct 17 that India has no plans to regulate or cap airfares in the free market under which airlines here operate under the new airfare policy being finalised. However, it will keep a “strong lever” on airlines to ensure they don’t resort to very sharp surges in “exceptional and extraordinary circumstances” that see demand rising for certain routes.
Article Summary: Supreme Court responds sharply to a plea highlighting a steep surge in airfares. Justice Vikram Nath tells the counsel, “Don’t travel by air. Next case,” before moving on to the next matter. India has adopted new airfare rules where government will not interfere.

Article Title: Days after Farooq’s Pak praise, Mehbooba says Abdullahs created distrust between Kashmir & rest of India
Article Text:
Mehbooba Mufti accuses NC of widening Kashmir’s divide with rest of India, urges Centre to hold talks.

SRINAGAR: Days after National Conference president Farooq Abdullah made a controversial statement hailing Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts on Kashmir , PDP president Mehbooba Mufti Monday launched an attack on the NC leadership across generations, accusing it of creating distrust between Kashmir and the rest of the country.Addressing party workers in Srinagar on PDP’s foundation day, she said: “NC’s policies, dating back to the days of Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, have created a wedge between Kashmir and the rest of the country. Unlike them, my father, Mufti Mohammad Sayeed, tried everything to bridge this gap.”“If there is any party that has betrayed Kashmiris, it is NC. As long as it remains in power, there will be no peace in Jammu & Kashmir,” Mehbooba said, urging party members to make efforts to regain power.She said if Kashmiris have suffered over the years, it was because of Sheikh Abdullah, who repeatedly changed his political positions, from supporting Kashmir’s accession to India to raising slogans for a plebiscite and Pakistan.Farooq was following in his father’s footsteps by recently stating that Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts were saving Kashmiris, portraying the neighbouring country as the “saviour” of Kashmiris.“This conveys a message to New Delhi that Kashmiris are with Pakistan and they should be oppressed, arrested and have their passports seized,” she said.“NC’s forte has been to defame Kashmiris since 1947,” she added.Targeting chief minister Omar Abdullah, she said he keeps blaming PDP for his failures, while he has failed to provide jobs to the people.The PDP chief also trained guns on the Union govt, accusing it of suppressing the voice of Kashmiris. She alleged that the Centre splintered her party after the abrogation of Article 370 , “but we are not among those who change political positions”.“The Govt of India must understand that the people of J&Kare the crown of India. If you trample upon this crown, you too will also suffer,” she said.“This is the land of rishis and peers (Sufi saints). If you do wrong to this land, you will not remain safe,” Mehbooba further said, adding: “How long will you govern us through suspicion? You must trust us the way (former prime minister) Atal Bihari Vajpayee trusted us.”She emphasised initiating talks, stating that Kashmiris will not be governed by force indefinitely.
Article Summary: Mehbooba Mufti accuses NC of widening Kashmir’s divide with rest of India, urges Centre to hold talks. “If there is any party that has betrayed Kashmiris, it is NC. As long as it remains in power, there will be no peace in Jammu & Kashmir,” she said.

Article Title: 'You became PM because of foreign help': Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi for debate
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday launched a scathing attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi , accusing him of becoming PM because of "foreign help".In a social media post on X, Rahul alleged that PM Modi's financial system was fully controlled and supported by foreigners, while foreign social media platforms fully backed him."Mr Modi, stop lying to this nation," the Congress leader said."You became PM because of foreign help. You remain PM because of foreign help. Your financial system is fully controlled and supported by foreigners. Foreign social media fully backs you," he added.Rahul also challenged PM Modi to an open debate on the issue, but said the latter would not dare to accept it."I challenge you to an open debate about this. Any stage, any time. Come if you have the guts. You won't dare, because you are terrified of what I know about you," he added.Rahul's remarks came in response to PM Modi's 'Ekta Diwas' speech, in which he accused the opposition of turning into an "obstructionist force" (avrodh paksh).The Prime Minister also warned against forces "engaged in conspiracies to divide" the country, saying social media was "being weaponised, rumours being spread, and attempts being made to tarnish India's image"."When the country was seeking solutions to external challenges, some forces within the country were also creating instability by spreading lies and rumours. But the countrymen stood shoulder to shoulder with the nation," PM Modi said“It is our misfortune that at this time in the country, the opposition has turned into an Avrodh Paksh rather than Virodh Paksh. In their frustration, these people are standing as obstacles in the way of the country’s development.This is not opposition; this is obstruction,” he added.In a veiled reference to Rahul's foreign trips, he said, “Due to the frustration of more than a decade, these people have now come out in the open. Who is secretly meeting whom abroad? Whom are the anti-India forces supporting? Who is speaking the language of India’s enemies? We will have to recognise all these patterns."
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday launched a scathing attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Rahul alleged that PM Modi's financial system was fully controlled and supported by foreigners. He also challenged PM Modi to an open debate on the issue, but said the latter would not dare to accept it.

Article Title: 'NCP united under Sunetra Pawar': Party rejects rift rumours as she skips Amit Shah meet

NCP leaders meet after Delhi parleys

NEW DELHI: The Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) on Monday sought to put speculation about an internal rift to rest, with party leaders dismissing reports of differences following a high-profile meeting between Union Home Minister Amit Shah and a delegation of senior NCP leaders in New Delhi.The speculation was fuelled by the absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay, from Sunday's meeting with Shah. The development raised questions about whether the party's leadership was being sidelined in discussions over its future following the death of Ajit Pawar NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil rejected reports suggesting that Sunetra Pawar and Rajya Sabha MP Parth Pawar had been excluded from the Delhi discussions, describing the claims as "incorrect, baseless and misleading".Patil accused sections of the media of giving the meeting an unnecessary political angle and creating an impression that the party was divided."Attempts are being made to give an unnecessary political twist to the meeting and create a narrative of internal differences and lack of coordination within the party. The NCP is an important constituent of the Mahayuti alliance and remains united under the leadership of Sunetra Pawar," he said.He also urged the media to verify information before reporting on the party."Do not politicise formal meetings between leaders of alliance partners. Speculation should not be portrayed as fact," the NCP leader added.The delegation that met Shah late on Sunday included Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Dilip Walse Patil, Hassan Mushrif, Chhagan Bhujbal and Dhananjay Munde.After returning to Maharashtra, the leaders held closed-door discussions at Bhujbal's residence. Walse Patil, who was part of the delegation, told PTI that all the leaders who had met Shah had returned to the state."The core group will meet now and DCM Sunetra Pawar in the evening," Walse Patil said.Patil said Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar had met Shah earlier to discuss issues facing the party after Ajit Pawar's death. During that meeting, she had informed Shah that a delegation of senior party leaders would meet him and requested an appointment."Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar had earlier met Shah and discussed various issues facing the party following the death of Ajit Pawar. During that meeting, she had informed Shah that a delegation of senior party leaders would meet him and requested him to give them time," Patil said.He added that the delegation comprised senior leaders familiar with key decisions taken during Ajit Pawar's tenure, issues concerning Maharashtra and matters related to the party.The meeting with Shah comes after a setback for the NCP, which recently lost the Aurangabad Graduates constituency in the Maharashtra Legislative Council elections, a seat it had held for 18 years.It has also been seeking the finance portfolio, which was held by Ajit Pawar until his death in a plane crash in January this year.Against this backdrop, the absence of Sunetra Pawar and her sons from the Delhi meeting added to questions about coordination and decision-making within the party.
Article Summary: NCP rejects reports of internal rift after meeting with Amit Shah. Speculation fuelled by absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay. NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil described the claims as "incorrect, baseless and misleading" He accused sections of the media of giving the meeting an unnecessary political angle.

Article Title: '2.5 lakh shops shut, Rs 10,000 crore loss': Delhi traders blame INDIA bloc rally for business disruption
Article Text:
Delhi traders claim Rs 10,000 crore loss as 2.5 lakh shops shut during INDIA bloc rally.

Traders had warned of business losses ahead of rally

Rahul's video appeal for participants to shop from local traders

INDIA bloc holds rally against SIR, alleged electoral irregularities

'Business boomed': Jairam Ramesh hits back at BJP over traders' loss claims

Amit Shah questions timing of rally, Rahul alleges shops shut in Delhi

NEW DELHI: Around 2.5 lakh shops across 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi remained closed on Sunday, with traders claiming losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season.Chamber of Trade & Industry (CTI) chairman Brijesh Goyal said nearly 80% of the approximately three lakh shops in markets surrounding the rally venue remained shut amid concerns over traffic restrictions, congestion and the expected arrival of large crowds.The disruption also affected the movement of customers, suppliers and dealers from towns surrounding the national capital. According to Goyal, around three lakh to four lakh people who regularly travel to Delhi for business did not arrive, while approximately 5,000 vehicles, including tempos and trucks, could not transport goods to markets in Old Delhi and Central Delhi.“Due to the rally held at Ramlila Maidan today, about 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity were affected. These historic markets house approximately 3,00,000 shops. Based on data we received this evening from various WhatsApp groups—comprising traders from different markets under the CTA (Confederation of All India Traders)—about 80% of these shops—roughly 2,50,000 out of 3,00,000—remained closed today,” he said.Goyal added that loading and unloading operations were disrupted, affecting wholesale and retail businesses during one of the busiest periods of the year.“The movement of goods—loading and unloading—was completely disrupted. During the peak Diwali season, these markets with individual turnovers collectively generate business worth approximately 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees. Even where shops remained open, sales were virtually non-existent; there were simply no customers,” he said.Putting the estimated losses at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, Goyal questioned who would compensate traders for the business disruption.“The question now arises: who will compensate for this loss, or who will make up for it—will the organisers do so?” he said.He said the timing of the rally had compounded the impact, as traders were preparing for the festive rush ahead of Dhanteras, scheduled four days later. Businesses in the affected markets depend heavily on the movement of customers and goods during this period.Ahead of the gathering, traders across several major commercial hubs in Delhi had opposed holding the rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season. They warned that traffic congestion and restrictions could disrupt wholesale markets and affect the livelihoods of thousands of daily-wage workers.The Automotive Parts Merchant Association (APMA), based at Kashmere Gate, said the rally's location could affect commercial activity across a three-kilometre radius, covering several major trading hubs in the capital.APMA president Vinay Narang said traders were not opposed to democratic protests but objected to the timing and choice of venue."We are not aligned with any political party, nor are we against democratic protests. But the timing and the venue are completely wrong. Ramlila Maidan is located in the middle of Asia’s largest commercial zone—with major markets like Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Daryaganj, Mori Gate, and Kashmere Gate within a three-kilometre radius," Narang said.Amid concerns raised by traders' associations, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people travelling to Delhi for the rally to support local businesses by shopping from their stores during the festive season.In a video message posted on X on Saturday, Gandhi urged participants to combine their participation in the protest with shopping from small businesses.“Tomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March. It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here,” Gandhi said.“Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,” he added.The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha also accused the BJP of spreading rumours about the rally's potential economic impact.“I know the rally will not harm the traders. The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours,” he said, adding, “But let's do both. Tomorrow there will be a march, there will be a rally, and lakhs of people will buy goods from the small shops of our traders.”The INDIA bloc held the rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging irregularities in the exercise.Several Opposition leaders attended the gathering, including Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Protesters also raised slogans such as "Vote chor, gaddi chhod", demanding accountability over alleged electoral irregularities.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Monday rejected claims that the INDIA bloc rally disrupted business in Delhi, alleging that the BJP's campaign warning of economic losses had been contradicted by increased shopping in local markets.In a post on X, Ramesh accused the BJP of spreading fear among traders and discouraging people from travelling to the national capital ahead of the rally. He said people arriving from different parts of the country were also expected to shop, benefiting businesses across Delhi."Every business operating in Delhi would benefit, directly or indirectly," he said.Ramesh alleged that the campaign was aimed at diverting attention from the Opposition's allegations of "vote theft" and protecting Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."But the exact opposite happened," he said.Claiming that Rahul Gandhi's appeal had received a positive response, Ramesh said wholesale markets in Old Delhi had opened and business had picked up, while small shopkeepers and street vendors had also benefited."The people of Delhi and those who came from across the country responded to this smear campaign in their own way. In response to Rahul Gandhi ji's appeal, people went shopping in Delhi's markets. Shops in the wholesale markets of Old Delhi opened, and business boomed. On top of that, people bought goods in abundance from small shopkeepers and street vendors too. Newspaper reports themselves are exposing the falsehood of this fake narrative," he said.Thanking traders, shopkeepers and Delhi residents, Ramesh said they had supported local businesses alongside the democratic protest."The BJP should understand that the voice of democracy cannot be suppressed by fear or smear campaigns," he said.His remarks came in contrast to the estimates shared by CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal, who claimed that traders had suffered losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, with around 2.5 lakh shops remaining closed.Earlier, Union Home Minister Amit Shah had criticised the Opposition over holding the rally during the festive shopping season, saying traders had repeatedly requested a postponement until after Diwali."Traders in Delhi pleaded with them, explaining that they have only one week in the entire year when the bulk of their business takes place. 'If we stock up on sweets and they don't sell, what happens? We suffer a loss. If we stock up on firecrackers and they don't sell, what happens? We suffer a loss...'" Shah said."The traders held press conferences--not once, but three times--wrote letters, and implored them to hold their rally after Diwali. But no—they insisted on holding their rally on that very day—the same dark day when the anti-Sikh riots, the Sikh massacre, took place," the Home Minister remarked.Before the rally, Rahul Gandhi had also accused the BJP of forcibly shutting shops in Delhi's Connaught Place and causing financial losses to local traders.In a post on X, Gandhi claimed that people attending the rally had been encouraged to support local businesses but found commercial establishments closed upon reaching the markets.
Article Summary: Traders claim Rs 10,000 crore loss as 2.5 lakh shops shut during INDIA bloc rally. Traders had warned of business losses ahead of rally. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people travelling to Delhi for the rally to support local businesses by shopping from stores during the festive season.

Article Title: Nita Ambani marks birthday with foundation stone ceremony for 5,000-person care facility
Article Text: Nita Ambani marked her birthday on Sunday by laying the foundation stone for a proposed 100-acre care township in Karjat, Maharashtra. The project, Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray, is envisioned as a lifelong home for more than 5,000 people, including orphaned children, senior citizens and people with developmental disabilities.Mukesh Ambani and members of the Ambani family attended the bhumi pujan and groundbreaking ceremony near Mumbai. The township, being established by Reliance Foundation, will be developed as a permanent, not-for-profit institution in phases. It is planned as a community with residential homes, healthcare facilities, schools, rehabilitation services and opportunities for education, work and recreation.Nita Ambani said the project was a step towards creating “a loving home for people with disabilities, children who need a home and seniors who seek care and comfort”. She said the township would combine medical support with the warmth of family life and give residents opportunities to learn, work, make friends and participate in festivals and celebrations.According to the plans shared by Reliance Foundation, the township will support a wider community of approximately 15,000 people, including residents, caregivers, medical professionals, support staff and their families.The proposed facility will comprise eight residential villages, each named after a sacred river of India. Residents will live in small, family-style homes supported by house parents and caregivers. Their rooms will be designed to offer familiarity and personal belonging, with residents encouraged to personalise their living spaces.The project will include a specialised hospital offering developmental medicine, epilepsy care, special-needs dentistry, palliative care and other medical services. Rehabilitation facilities for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and hydrotherapy are also planned.Other proposed amenities include a temple, gardens, farms, playgrounds, workshops, cafés and inclusive sports and recreational facilities. An animal companionship farm is expected to be developed with expertise from Vantara.The township will also offer vocational training and employment opportunities through facilities such as a bakery, café and craft studios. A dedicated training academy for disability-care professionals, a hospice wing and a garden of remembrance are also part of the plans.The initiative is expected to have an impact beyond the township. Around 1,000 people from nearby areas are expected to access therapy, education and employment opportunities, while respite-care facilities, mobile medical clinics and outreach programmes will support families in neighbouring districts.
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani and members of the Ambani family attended the bhumi pujan and groundbreaking ceremony near Mumbai. The township will be developed as a permanent, not-for-profit institution in phases. It is planned as a community with residential homes, healthcare facilities, schools, rehabilitation services and opportunities for education, work and recreation.

Article Title: India, Israel vote against Pakistan-backed UN arms control resolution: What it means
Article Text:
In a significant move, India and Israel opposed a UN resolution proposed by Pakistan and Belarus concerning regional arms control.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view How effective do you think regional arms control efforts are in ensuring global security? Very effective Somewhat effective Not effective 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

India and Israel have voted against a Pakistan- and Belarus-sponsored draft resolution at the united nations seeking conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels, with New Delhi arguing that national security concerns cannot be restricted by geographical boundaries.The draft resolution, titled ‘General and complete disarmament: Conventional arms control at the regional and subregional levels’, was adopted by the UN general assembly’s First Committee on Monday, receiving 180 votes in favour, two against and no abstentions.According to the news agency PTI, India and Israel were the only two countries among the 193 UN member states to oppose the resolution.Explaining India's position, Anmol Sher Bedi, first secretary at India's permanent mission to the UN, maintained that conventional arms control was a global issue and should not be addressed primarily through regional and subregional frameworks.“We are not fully convinced that it should be pursued primarily in regional and sub-regional contexts,” Bedi said while presenting India's explanation of vote before the UNGA first committee.He added that New Delhi's opposition was in line with its consistent position on the matter.India also raised questions over the resolution's call for the UN disarmament commission to develop principles that could provide a framework for regional agreements on conventional arms control.“We read this request with a certain degree of curiosity,” Bedi said, pointing out that the commission had already reached three consensus-based outcomes on related issues.These included guidelines and recommendations on regional disarmament adopted in 1993, guidelines on conventional arms control and disarmament finalised in 1999, and recommendations on practical confidence-building measures concerning conventional weapons agreed upon in 2017.“That makes three consensus outcomes on this very subject in the very body now being asked to start from scratch,” he said.Questioning the need for further discussions, Bedi said it was difficult to understand why an issue that had already undergone extensive deliberations needed to be taken up again, unless the intention was to keep the UN's disarmament machinery occupied.India also criticised the resolution's emphasis on maintaining a balance in defence capabilities within regional and subregional settings.Bedi argued that the approach wrongly presumed that countries' security interests were confined to their immediate geographical neighbourhoods.“This assumes that the security concerns of States politely stop at their regional borders. They do not,” he said.He further stressed that national security considerations often extend beyond narrowly defined regional boundaries, adding that the idea of maintaining a military balance within a particular region or subregion was unrealistic.The resolution argues that conventional arms control should primarily be pursued at regional and subregional levels, as most threats to international peace and security in the post-Cold War period have emerged among countries within the same geographical regions.It also calls for promoting agreements that strengthen regional peace and security while maintaining armaments and military forces at the lowest possible levels.Separately, India voted against a paragraph referring to conventional arms control proposals concerning South Asia.The paragraph took note of initiatives undertaken in various regions, including consultations among certain latin American countries and proposals for conventional arms control in South Asia, while acknowledging the importance of such measures for regional security.The resolution further states that militarily significant countries and nations possessing greater military capabilities have a special responsibility to advance agreements aimed at strengthening regional peace and security.
Article Summary: India and Israel voted against a Pakistan- and Belarus-sponsored draft resolution at the united nations seeking conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels. New Delhi argued that national security concerns cannot be restricted by geographical boundaries. The draft resolution was adopted by the UN general assembly’s First Committee on Monday.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said no protest group can occupy a designated demonstration site indefinitely, observing that the right to protest must be balanced with the rights of other citizens. Hearing pleas filed by traders' associations over the impact of demonstrations in Delhi, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said designated protest venues must be made available to different groups for specific periods."You can't occupy a site for all times. Where farmers, journalists, etc. will go? Everyone has right to protest. Designated time must be given for designated period," CJI Surya Kant said, according to LiveLaw.The bench also said that orders granting permission for protests must clearly specify the reasons for allowing or refusing them. "You can't prevent other people, that I am doing protest now you can't," the CJI observed.The court was hearing pleas raising concerns over alleged police brutality, mass detentions, the closure of Metro stations and internet shutdowns during protests, besides the impact of demonstrations on businesses.A traders' counsel told the court that around 50 lakh people lived in areas surrounding the protest site and claimed that shops remained shut, with virtually nobody visiting Connaught Place. The court issued notices to the Centre and other authorities on a plea by the Kirana Committee Delhi seeking a halt to protests during the festive season.However, the bench said it could not adjudicate the traders' grievances unless all organisations involved in the protests were made parties to the proceedings. It asked the traders' associations to implead the organisers of the anti-CEC protests.The hearing comes weeks after the Centre de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, identifying Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as alternative venues for demonstrations.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said designated protest venues must be made available to different groups for specific periods. The bench also said that orders granting permission for protests must clearly specify the reasons for allowing or refusing them. The court issued notices to the Centre and other authorities on a plea by the Kirana Committee Delhi seeking a halt to protests.

NEW DELHI: SP leader and ten time MLA Azam Khan on Monday moved Supreme Court challenging the ED decision to arrest him on stepping out of Rampur jail after Allahabad HC granted him bail in the last of the 95 cases, which have been slapped on him after BJP came to power in Uttar Pradesh in 2017.Advocate Mohd Nizamuddin Pasha told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the arrest by ED in a 2019 case, in which FIR itself was registered 13 years after the allegations about land purchase transactions fo Jauhar University from farmers, was illegal.Though the bench initially asked Khan why he did not move the Allahabad HC, it agreed to list the matter for hearing. He has been acquitted in six cases, and three cases were closed after his complicity could not be proved.“He has been convicted in six; in four of these his sentence has been suspended and/or his conviction stayed, and in the other two, the sentence of two years has been undergone.The remaining 80 cases are pending trial. Article Title: 'Everything is available': SC flags open sale of firecrackers in Delhi despite restrictions

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday flagged the alleged open sale of conventional and uncertified firecrackers in Delhi markets despite its recent order allowing only certified green crackers ahead of Diwali.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale referred to a media report published on Tuesday, which highlighted the availability of different varieties of firecrackers in several markets across the national capital, according to Bar and Bench.The bench asked Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati to look into the alleged violations."In today's report, there's a photograph, they say that notwithstanding yesterday's order, now everything is available in the (firecracker) shops. Please look into it," Justice Sundresh told Bhati.The judge also referred to the report's claims that licensed and unlicensed crackers, including those with and without QR codes, were being sold openly."They say that in the market every other cracker, licensed, unlicensed, QR code, or no QR code, everything is available. Please take a note of it," he said.Also read: SC on Diwali: Crackers on Nov 7-8 in 2 time slots, and keep it green On November 2, the Supreme Court allowed the sale of certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR from November 4 to 6 and their use on November 7 and 8, subject to restrictions.Firecrackers can be burst only between 6am and 7am and 8pm and 10pm on these two days. A complete ban will be restored from November 9.The court had clarified that only firecrackers certified by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) and the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) could be manufactured and sold.It also restricted sales to designated locations and prohibited online sales. Each box must carry a product-specific QR code to verify its certification. The manufacture of firecracker strings, or laris, and crackers containing barium was also prohibited.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday flagged the alleged open sale of conventional and uncertified firecrackers in Delhi markets. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale referred to a media report published on Tuesday. The judge also referred to the report's claims that licensed and unlicensed crackers, including those with and without QR codes, were being sold openly.

Article Title: Rouse Avenue court seeks Delhi Police response on Bimol Akoijam's anticipatory bail plea

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue Court on Tuesday issued notice to Delhi Police on the anticipatory bail plea of Manipur MP and former Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor Bimol Akoijam in a sexual harassment case and extended his interim protection till November 5.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought the police response and directed the investigating agency to place on record the complaint filed by JNU students against Akoijam. The matter has been listed for arguments on November 5.Akoijam is seeking anticipatory bail in an FIR registered at Vasant Kunj North police station following allegations of sexual harassment levelled by 11 JNU students against him when he was working as a professor at the university.Additional Public Prosecutor Manish Rawat appeared for Delhi Police and accepted the notice. The police have already filed a reply before the Patiala House Court.During the hearing, Akoijam's counsel submitted that the complaint was made by a group of students to the dean and not by any aggrieved woman directly. The counsel also said the university's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) had examined the matter and its report had been annexed to the bail application.The defence further submitted that Akoijam had cooperated with the investigation and appeared before the investigating officer, while the alleged complainant was not joining the probe. The counsel also pointed out that the high court had stayed his termination from the university.Akoijam had initially secured transit anticipatory bail from a Manipur court on October 12, which was extended till October 20 and subsequently till October 29.He then approached the Patiala House Court, which granted him interim protection till November 2. However, the court held that it could not hear his anticipatory bail plea as he is a sitting MP, and that the matter fell within the jurisdiction of the Rouse Avenue Court.The investigating officer had also opposed the plea on the jurisdictional ground. Following the transfer of the case, Akoijam moved the Rouse Avenue Court for anticipatory bail.
Article Summary: Akoijam is seeking anticipatory bail in an FIR registered at Vasant Kunj North police station. He is accused of sexual harassment levelled by 11 JNU students against him. The matter has been listed for arguments on November 5.

Article Title: NHAI to use desilted river material for road projects in Bihar, says transport minister Gadkari
Article Text:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has embarked on an innovative project to leverage materials from Bihar's rivers for highway development

The national highways authority of India (NHAI) will use sand and other materials excavated from rivers and water bodies in Bihar for highway construction, union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari said after the Bihar government and the road transport ministry signed an MoU.Nitin Gadkari said the initiative would also help mitigate flooding in the state.The Bihar chief minister said the state faces floods not only due to its own water but also because of water flowing in from other regions, including Nepal. He noted that the highest flood levels (HFL) had risen in three rivers despite Bihar receiving less rainfall this year.Desilting rivers and water bodies could help reduce the impact of floods, the chief minister said, adding that desilting the Ganga and reclaiming land along its banks could create space for one lakh Ganga-facing homes.
Article Summary: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) will use sand and other materials excavated from rivers and water bodies in Bihar for highway construction. Nitin Gadkari said the initiative would also help mitigate flooding in the state. Desilting the Ganga and reclaiming land along its banks could create space for one lakh Ganga-facing homes.

Article Title: 'Rs 25cr spent on ads to claim no stubble burning, FIRs tell another story': BJP targets AAP govt in Punjab
Article Text:
Rs 20-25 crore was spent on advertisements to project that there was no stubble burning in the state, said

Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Tuesday accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab of allowing and facilitating stubble burning while spending Rs 20-25 crore on advertisements claiming that no farm fires were taking place in the state. He alleged that the government was then registering FIRs against farmers for stubble burning, even as it publicly denied the practice.He also questioned the appointment of former AAP spokesperson Reena Gupta as chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board, alleging that the move was aimed at manipulating pollution data.Addressing a press conference in Delhi, Sirsa claimed that Punjab had recorded more than 1,000 incidents of stubble burning and alleged that the state government was trying to conceal the extent of the problem through publicity campaigns.“Advertisements worth Rs 20-25 crore were released to claim that stubble burning was not taking place in Punjab this year. On the other hand, I am handing over copies of all the FIRs, district-wise, to you. These are all FIRs registered in connection with stubble burning,” he said, displaying documents that he claimed contained details of the cases, further alleging that "Punjab Police and Punjab government officers are facilitating the burning of stubble.Taking aim at AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Sirsa alleged that the party had brought its political spokesperson from Delhi to head the Punjab Pollution Control Board to influence the reporting of pollution data.“For the first time in Punjab's history, a non-Punjabi, non-IAS, non-technical person has been appointed to such a position. They have appointed their political spokesperson, who is said to be a close relative of Arvind Kejriwal, as the chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board after bringing her from Delhi,” Sirsa said.He identified the appointee as Reena Gupta, alleging that she was being projected as the face of the campaign to deny the scale of stubble burning in Punjab. Sirsa claimed the appointment was intended to “conceal the truth by fudging data”.Sirsa sought to contrast Punjab's situation with Delhi's air quality, claiming that the national capital had recorded 220 clean-air days in 2026, the highest in a decade. He also said October was the cleanest in the past 10 years and that the average air quality index (AQI) had improved by 10 per cent compared with previous years.Appealing to Kejriwal and AAP leader Manish Sisodia not to undermine Delhi's efforts to improve air quality, Sirsa said, “By setting fires in Punjab, you are once again causing the situation in Delhi to deteriorate.”
Article Summary: Manjinder Singh Sirsa accuses Punjab government of allowing and facilitating stubble burning while spending Rs 20-25 crore on advertisements. He also questioned the appointment of former AAP spokesperson Reena Gupta as chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board. Sirsa claimed the appointment was intended to “conceal the truth by fudging data”
